Subject: Production latency spike + 5xxs on checkout (Feb 18)

Jonas / Hannah —

We hit a severe latency spike and elevated 5xxs that started ~09:52 PST and lasted ~12 minutes during our peak checkout surge. Checkout latency (p95) jumped from ~600ms to ~6.1s, and ~8% of inbound requests returned 500/502. This impacted several customers who reported failed purchases.

We've pulled a few example request ids and attached a short log bundle (request-ids included below). Can you confirm if a config change or model variant rollout happened around that timeframe? We need an RCA and ETA for mitigation steps by EOD.

Example request ids attached: swc-req-2314, swc-req-2319, swc-req-2330

Thanks,
Maya Singh

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 5xxs on checkout (Feb 18) — preliminary findings

Team —

Prelim root cause summary (investigation running):
1) Around 09:50 PST a new autoscaling heuristic landed in prod that tightened the per-GPU request batching window (change was deployed as part of INF-4528).
2) Under sudden traffic burst the shortened batch window prevented efficient batching and increased KV cache miss rates for long-context sessions (checkout flow).
3) Higher kernel launch frequency + cache churn led to CPU scheduling pressure on the shard handling the checkout route, causing tokenization timeouts and 5xxs.

Mitigation performed (09:58 PST): reverted the autoscaling heuristic and re-enabled the previous batching window. Error rate dropped and p95 returned to baseline by 10:04 PST.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- [Marcus] Produce a reproducible load test that mimics the checkout token sequence and validate batching/window behavior (ETA: 24h).
- [Hannah] Approve an emergency canary rule so we can opt-out models/routes from the heuristic until we validate under heavy tail (ETA: 2h).
- [Jonas] Coordinate a customer-facing summary and schedule a readout with SwiftCommerce for tomorrow (ETA: EOD today).
- [Lauren] Create an action tracker (sheet) with owners and closure dates; include mitigation verification steps and post-deploy QA (ETA: 4h).

I've attached the debug snapshot and a zipped chunk of request traces we captured.

Attachments: request-logs-20270218.zip, debug-snapshot-20270218.tar.gz

2) Short-term mitigations taken and evidence (metrics/screenshots).

4) Verification criteria for the mitigation (load test targets, pass/fail thresholds).

Subject: SwiftCommerce incident summary (Feb 18) + RCA and action tracker

Maya / Alex —

Thank you again for patience while we completed the investigation. Attached is the formal RCA and our action tracker showing owners, deadlines, and verification criteria. TL;DR: a recent autoscaling batching heuristic change reduced effective batching under bursty traffic, which increased KV cache misses and kernel startup overhead for the checkout route. We reverted the change immediately and validated recovery.

What's included:
- swiftcommerce-RCA-20270218.pdf — one-page executive RCA and timeline.
- action-tracker-sheet.csv — owners and hard deadlines (linked to Jira INF-4621).
- request-logs-20270218.zip — raw traces we used to reproduce behavior.

Key commitments:
- Reproducible load test and validation run (Marcus) — complete by 2027-02-19 23:59 PST.
- Canary rule to opt routes out of the heuristic (Hannah / Infra) — deployment by 2027-02-20 18:00 PST.
- Post-deploy verification and customer QA run (Lauren / SwiftCommerce) — scheduled week of 2027-02-22.

We propose a short 30-minute readout tomorrow at 10:00 PST to walk the RCA and walk through the tracker; please reply with any availability conflicts. If you'd prefer the executive one-pager only (no walkthrough) we can deliver that immediately.

Apologies for the disruption — we recognize the impact on your checkout conversions and are treating this as a high-priority operational improvement.

Best,
Jonas Weber
